system_description.narrative_title: Energy shocks, regional wars, and US-driven strategic unpredictability
system_description.narrative_summary: The open system is defined by overlapping security crises (Iran‑led Gulf escalation, the Russia‑Ukraine war, and persistent Israel‑Palestine violence) that feed commodity shocks and shipping chokepoints, which in turn amplify financial-market stress. U.S. domestic politics and an interventionist, unpredictable executive posture (military threats, tariff actions, changes to alliance drills) are reshaping alliance behaviour and de‑risking patterns, accelerating strategic realignments. Simultaneously China’s economic slowdown and industrial/tech decoupling pressures create supply‑chain frictions that interact with capital‑market volatility, producing feedback loops across energy, trade and fiscal stability.
system_description.scope: States, alliances and major non‑state actors; regional conflict theaters (Middle East, Eastern Europe, Korea); strategic sea lanes and energy infrastructure; global commodity markets (oil, gas, metals); international capital and bond markets; multinational corporations and supply chains; diplomatic and institutional responses.
system_description.super_system: The globalized political‑economic system (planetary order linking states, markets, transport networks and ecological constraints).
adjacent_subsystems: Middle East security–energy nexus (Iran, GCC, Red Sea/Hormuz shipping)
Global financial and sovereign debt markets (bond yields, fiscal stress)

variables.name: Iran–Gulf maritime confrontation
variables.description: Iran, the United States and Gulf states are locked in a widening confrontation that is disrupting Strait of Hormuz shipping and regional commerce through missile and tanker attacks, diplomatic ruptures and escalating retaliatory threats.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain engaged in a high‑intensity, attritional war characterized by long‑range strikes, massed drone operations and Western arms and sanctions that are reshaping battlefield dynamics and domestic pressures in the belligerents.

variables.name: US–China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are accelerating strategic decoupling across technology, trade and supply chains as tariffs, export controls, investment screens and industrial policy reconfigure global markets and corporate strategies.

variables.name: US alliance credibility in Asia
variables.description: Questions about Washington’s defense commitments and force posture—manifest in cuts to joint drills and mixed signals toward Korea, Japan and other partners—are straining alliances in East Asia and prompting allied reappraisals of deterrence and burden‑sharing.

variables.name: Israel–Palestine violent escalation
variables.description: Israel, Palestinian armed groups and proximate regional actors are locked in an intensifying cycle of strikes, ground operations and political manoeuvres that is deepening the humanitarian crisis and reshaping regional alignments.
